Under the general supervision of the Cal-Bridge Assistant Director for Administration and Finance, the Cal-Bridge Undergraduate Program Coordinator independently provides a broad range of support in the following primary functional areas:

The Program Coordinator serves as a central operational lead, ensuring the efficient execution of program objectives. This role manages day-to-day administrative operations, coordinates logistics for events and workshops, and oversees participant compliance and support systems. The successful candidate will act as a key liaison between program leadership, stakeholders, and contributing to the continuous improvement of program processes.
Essential Functions:

The identification of essential functions below is not intended to be an exhaustive list of all duties that may be assigned to this position, nor does it restrict the duties which may be assigned to this position if such duties reasonably relate to the position.

Program Operations & Administration *Maintain master project calendars, tracking overlapping deadlines and coordinating with leadership to implement strategic plans. *Manage program documentation, including contracts, handbooks, forms, and instructional manuals, ensuring materials are current and accessible. *Facilitate internal communication by disseminating information to stakeholders, managing mailing lists, and scholar information systems *Draft emails, flyers, updates, newsletter and website content *Contribute to marketing efforts and maintain program website content. *Develop and implement systems, surveys, and workflows to improve operational efficiency and track program metrics. *Provide training to staff on program processes, databases, and software. *Oversee participant progress tracking, including managing transcript reviews, academic progress meetings, and disciplinary reporting where necessary. *Serve as the primary point of contact for participant inquiries, providing guidance on program requirements and policies. *Administer support programs, such as financial support requests, tutoring hours, and mentorship programs, ensuring accurate data entry and timely processing. *Support recruitment efforts by maintaining relationships with external liaisons, mentors, and partner organizations. *Schedule and support committee meetings, including preparing agendas, gathering materials, and recording action items. *Assist in the preparation of annual progress reports and funding requests. *Ensure all program activities comply with institutional, state, and federal regulations (e.g., funding agency requirements). 40%

Event & Workshop Coordination *Assist with planning and executing program events, orientations, and workshops, including participant and location logistics, venue booking, vendor management, and catering arrangements. *Manage complex logistics for attendees, including travel arrangements, lodging, reimbursements, and on-site troubleshooting. *Coordinate materials for events, including speaker outreach, slide deck updates, abstract collection, and the creation of event booklets. *Ensure smooth on-site operations, including accessibility logistics, signage, and equipment setup. 35%

Financial Management Coordinate with attendees and process all event reimbursements. *Coordinate and process scholar and participant stipends. *Process financial transactions, including travel, submitting purchase orders, vendor insurance, and catering payments. 25%
This is a fully remote position, and the selected candidate must be able to work successfully from a home/remote office and be able to fulfill the requirements of the UCI telecommuting agreement.
Selected candidate will be required to complete training within established time frames as directed including UC compliance training.

Strong organizational and planning skills, including the ability to set priorities, maintain workflow, meet deadlines for simultaneous projects, and complete a high volume of work with attention to detail and accuracy with frequent interruptions.
Demonstrated ability to set and maintain a positive, collaborative, open, "can-do" environment.
Demonstrated analytical, problem solving and decision-making skills, while exercising flexibility, initiative and discretion.
Familiarity with University personnel policies and procedures.

Financial management and accounting skills. Familiarity with generally accepted accounting principles, funding accounting, internal control standards, and/or audit principles. Ability to learn federal and state funding policies and procedures.
Ability to work with diverse groups to achieve results.
Ability to learn and use new systems and software programs.
Strong interpersonal and customer-service skills. Ability to work with and support Faculty, Staff, and scholars.
Strong verbal and written communication skills to convey information clearly, concisely, and accurately.
Ability to work independently.
Ability to work as part of a team.
Ability to work long periods of time at a computer with or without accommodation.
This position requires the ability to report to campus to work in-person as operationally required, with reasonable notice as determined by your manager.
Ability to work occasional evenings and weekends as directed.
Ability to travel to multiple work locations on and off campus.
Ability to travel within a defined regional or service area.
Ability to maintain appearance and conduct suitable for working in a professional setting.
